rows.evidence: Q1: Materials and methods - three-year greenhouse field trial (2019-2021) in Yangling with CK, FP and IF treatments in randomized blocks. Q2: Results 'Ambient temperature and irrigation rates' and Table 6 - sensor-controlled drip fertigation (IF) used 61-92 mm vs 97.5-136 mm under farmers' drip fertigation, saving 29-37% of irrigation water, and IWUE was significantly higher (61-73% increase) with no yield penalty and higher nutrient use efficiency. Q4: Figs 7-9 and Discussion - root length, surface area, tips and volume were measured and found significantly greater under IF, and were positively correlated with IWUE and nutrient use efficiency; soil water content was continuously monitored with FDR sensors as the control variable.
rows.notes: All treatments used drip fertigation; the comparison is sensor-controlled (intelligent) drip fertigation vs farmers' conventional drip fertigation, not drip vs another irrigation method. Taken as evidence for the passage's point about precise water supply and efficient water/fertilizer use under drip fertigation, but it does not isolate drip itself. Single site, single crop, plot scale, one measurement method. Q7: the discussion notes high cost as an obstacle and that control parameters met crop demand, but no condition is stated as a requirement from the findings. Q8: no limitations of the result are stated. Q9: only Tukey letter groupings and percentage differences are reported in the text; no SD/CI visible.

notes: Text lacks tables and figures; reference list absent. Soil water content monitored by sensors is not reported as a result.
